title: ms-gateway-api Ocelot timeouts proxying to microservices.methodlocal.int (sync-util / preferences / account paths)

any_of.contains: Unusual number of XHR errors for account

diagnosis: Frontend XHR errors (status_code:0, 'Failed to load') reported to DataDog RUM by method-ui are symptoms — the actual failure happens upstream in ms-gateway-api's Ocelot ResponderMiddleware, which raises RequestTimedOutError / TaskCanceledException while waiting for microservices.methodlocal.int (the .NET Framework Tier-3 IIS pool) to respond. Affected paths span multiple owned services on that pool: /syncutil/syncwidget/{account}/GetSyncWidgetInfoAsync, /preferences/v3/User, /account/learning/progress, /account/banners/queue. The pattern is chronic — Ocelot warning volume in the 17:00 UTC hour was 1072 today vs 1064 24h ago (+0.7%), so the underlying timeout rate is steady-state, not a regression. DataDog monitor 77419271 ('Unusual number of XHR errors for account: {{@account_name.name}}') trips whenever a single account's user session bunches >40 such XHR errors within 5 min, which happens randomly across the user base as long as gateway→microservices latency stays at chronic levels.
playbook: 1) Confirm chronic baseline by comparing ES Ocelot.Responder.Middleware Warning volume in the alert window vs the same window 24h ago — if delta < 20%, it's the chronic pattern (no new incident). 2) Aggregate timeouts by RequestPath: if dominant paths are all under upstream microservices.methodlocal.int, it's pool-level. 3) Identify which downstream microservice owns the slow path via Ocelot config in ms-gateway-api/gateway/API/ocelot.*.json. 4) Decision tree for the fix: (a) raise per-route Ocelot timeout (cheapest, masks symptom — appropriate if Ben prefers user-facing reliability over visibility), (b) scale microservices IIS pool / shorten recycle interval (medium cost, addresses cold-start tail), (c) profile the upstream microservice (sync-util / preferences / account) under prod load to find the slow path — root-cause fix but expensive. 5) Once Ben picks an option, update fix_status from 'needs-ops-decision' to 'proposed'/'in-progress' and add fix_jira.
